title: A PD4 group without an aspherical manifold model
main_claim: There is a finitely presented integral PD4 group G with a finite 4-dimensional K(G,1) that is not the fundamental group of any closed aspherical topological 4-manifold. G comes from the Davis reflection of a smooth chamber D. D has free fundamental group and a hyperbolic pi_2 basis, and its marked boundary S admits no graph-type topological filling, which is imported from the companion paper's tensor obstruction. If a manifold model M existed, then KL surgery, Quinn's stable product theorem and a 'direction-control' replacement for goodness would produce such a filling.

issues.description: The whole contradiction depends on the companion paper TO (Prop 6.1, Thm 3.1, Thm 5.1, Prop 4.5/5.2) being applicable to an arbitrary marked topological W with the graph type of X. That includes the punctured-form lemma standing in for vertex smoothness. The transfer is argued only in outline. The claim implies that free groups are not good, which is an extraordinary consequence.
issues.evidence: 'This is precisely the argument of Lemma 2.5 ... of [TO], now applied to the marked W rather than requiring a homeomorphism W=X'; Lemma ch:puncture-forms asserts without detail that the source's gauge, holonomy and formal-lift steps go through.

issues.description: Phase 2 separates arbitrarily many upper components inside one colour neighbourhood using a single extra height raise. It cites FQ's collection-separation procedure, but that procedure is stated with a bounded number of collections. Containment and the height budget for an unbounded number of collections are asserted, not checked. The claim looks plausible, because push-offs stay in neighbourhoods of already-present images, but it is not verified.
issues.evidence: 'There may be arbitrarily many of them. The height is raised once more inside that neighborhood ... No estimate depending on their number is needed'

issues.location: Lemma ct:directions (comparison of direction map with the classifying map)
issues.description: The key nullity statement is proved only in sketch: a loop in Z whose direction image lies in a contractible patch is null. I reconstructed it as follows. Extend beta∘rho∘eta over the central core by c. That map kills the noncentral chamber groups and is the identity on the central factor, so it is homotopic to the projection classifying map. Peeling is compatible via the pinch. The reconstruction works, but the paper leaves these steps implicit.
issues.evidence: 'In a noncentral chamber the gallery map collapses its inner part ... The induced homomorphism is thus exactly the projection retaining the central factor.'

issues.description: The paper says that phi^{-1}∘f has trivial normal invariant, which treats normal invariants as subtracting under composition. The composition formula actually carries a pullback twist. Because phi is a pinch self-equivalence acting trivially on pi_1 and pi_2, the conclusion is still fine.
issues.evidence: 'Thus phi^{-1}∘f has trivial normal invariant and the same marking as f.'

sibling_notes: Siblings in family 305 audited the companions 'A marked tensor obstruction...' (rank 281) and 'A boundary-only obstruction...' (rank 217). Both returned no_gap_found and flagged the claim as extraordinary because it implies F2 is not good. This paper imports the TO marked geometry, Prop 6.1 and Thm 3.1, so its correctness for part (3) of the chamber proposition is inherited from those. The new content is the reflection/KL/stable-product transfer and the direction-control bypass of goodness in Section 4, and I found no failing step in either.
